Subject: Clarifying MediGroup purge windows and log-retention exceptions

Hi Nisha / legal team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To make sure we capture everything for the DPA amendment and the subprocessor checklist, can you confirm the following points so we can put a clear timeline into the DocuSign amendment?

- Preferred primary deletion window for customer-initiated erasures (e.g., how fast after a request should primary data be removed from the online store?)
- Desired maximum backup purge timeframe (are you asking for 30, 60, or 90 days for cold backups before purge?)
- Any telemetry/log categories you expect to be exempt from standard purge (e.g., aggregate telemetry retained for 180 days for incident investigation)
- Cross-border key handling: do you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms) for EU-origin data?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the questions we discussed so legal can mark preferred options: MediGroup_DPA_questions.xlsx (attachment).

If you confirm these points we'll draft the amendment with the phased purge language we discussed and loop in Marissa for legal redline.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Clarifying MediGroup purge windows and log-retention exceptions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks — I filled out the spreadsheet and added a few clarifications inline. High level answers:

- Primary deletion: we expect deletions from the primary store within 48 hours of an authenticated erase request.
- Backups: MediGroup prefers a 90-day backup purge window for full backups; however we need a 30-day hot-restore period (immediate restore capability) followed by 60 days cold-only that can only be restored via a retrieval request and audit trail.
- Logs/telemetry: we need certain security/incident logs (auth events, admin changes, system errors) retained for 180 days for investigation and M&A diligence exceptions.
- Keys: For EU-sourced PHI we prefer BYOK; for US-only data Redwood-managed keys are OK if you provide key access logs and HSM attestation.

I've attached our subprocessor list we cross-checked: MG_DPA_Subprocessors.csv. Legal ops copied for visibility — we may request SOC2 evidence for the most sensitive subprocessors.

Can you draft the phased purge clause and a short runbook for evidence retention so we can confirm?

Regards,
Nisha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MediGroup Health

Actionable items from our side:
1) I'll draft a phased purge clause that specifies: 0–30 days hot-restore, 31–90 days cold-only with a 14-day rollback buffer before final purge; primary store deletion within 48 hours.
2) Marissa, tagging you to draft the DPA amendment/redline to include: subprocessor attestations, evidence list (SOC2 reports), and exception handling for the 180-day telemetry retention.
3) Karthik, could you confirm whether Redwood can provide daily purge run logs (hash of purged objects + timestamp + operator id) and whether we can expose a read-only evidence bucket to MediGroup auditors?

I'll include the requested language in the amendment and circulate a redline by end of day Friday.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Draft redline — phased purge & telemetry exception language

Hi all,

I reviewed Priyom's proposed language and added redline comments in the attached document (redline_DPA_Medigroup.docx). High-level suggestions:

- Accept the 48-hour primary deletion, but clarify that deletion from the primary store may be delayed for lawfulhold/processing reasons with customer notice and case id.
- For backups: incorporate a phased purge schedule: 0–30d hot-restore (immediate), 31–90d cold-restore subject to authenticated retrieval request + audit; final purge at day 91 unless legal hold applies.
- For the 180-day telemetry exception: define a narrow schema of telemetry retained (auth events, admin audit logs, incident traces) and require an owner+purpose for retention. No content-level user data should be retained beyond the standard window unless separately authorized.
- Subprocessor attestations: require SOC2 Type II or equivalent for any subprocessor with access to plaintext customer content; others require an annual security questionnaire.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide purge-run manifests (object id hashes + purge timestamp + purge job id) and a daily summary export to a secure evidence bucket; we should agree retention of those manifests for 365 days.

Nisha — please confirm you can accept the manifest format and 365-day evidence retention for audit purposes. Also advise whether MediGroup needs direct access or periodic reports.

Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_DPA_Medigroup.docx
From: Nisha Kapoor <nisha.kapoor@medigroup.com>

Cc: legal.ops@medigroup.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 13:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redline — phased purge & telemetry exception language

Marissa — thanks, the redlines look sensible. A few follow-ups:

1) Evidence access — MediGroup prefers periodic push reports (weekly manifests) to our secure S3 ingestion with a separate read-only role rather than continuous direct access.
2) Manifest format — confirmed: object id hash + purge job id + timestamp + operator id + retention-policy-tag is sufficient.
3) Telemetry exception — we will limit requests to the categories you listed; please add a mechanism for MediGroup to request extension (with justification) and automated notification when an exception expires.

We will prepare DocuSign sign-off once Redwood confirms the weekly push and the 365-day evidence manifest retention. I've attached a short PDF with the exact fields legal ops will expect: requested_evidence_list.pdf.

Regards,
Nisha

- Redwood accepts the phased purge language (0–30d hot, 31–90d cold with 14d rollback buffer) and 48-hour primary deletion window; lawful holds will be honored with customer notice.
- Redwood will produce weekly manifest pushes to MediGroup's secure S3 ingestion endpoint; manifest retention on Redwood side = 365 days.
- Telemetry exception process: requests via support ticket + justification; automated reminder 7 days before exception expiry; MediGroup may request an extension with approval flow documented in the amendment.
- Subprocessor requirements: SOC2 Type II or equivalent for any subprocessor accessing plaintext; Redwood will supply SOC2 links or attestations for the named subprocessors in MG_DPA_Subprocessors.csv.

Next items: I will upload the redlined amendment to the Drive folder and create a DocuSign envelope for signatures (link below). Marissa will perform a final pass and we aim to have this with your legal ops for signature by EOD Wed.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MediGroup-DPA

If that schedule works, I'll set a 30-minute sync Wed to walk through the manifest format and S3 ingestion details.

Best,
Priyom
